pr.title: Lowercase repository names as the panel reads them
pr.head: 0e8a8a5b76dcb2fa3f81873a32b43c4746244eff

summary: The Projector panel is the list of pull requests that Claude Code shows above the prompt. It names each row #12 when every row belongs to one repository, and adds the repository's name when they do not. It decides that by counting the distinct repo strings among its rows.

GitHub ignores case in owner and repository names, so o/r and O/R are one repository. The panel kept whatever spelling each source used, though. When one session subscribed to O/R#2 and another tracked o/r#1, the panel counted two repositories and labelled the rows r#1 and R#2. It also sent GitHub one query per spelling.
This change lowercases the repository at the three readers that every panel row comes from:

• parseTracked reads an earlier watcher's tracked file, one owner/repo#number per line.
  • parseSubscriptions reads the session's subscriptions file, which the CLI writes.
  • parseAdopted reads the pull requests that the watch daemon adopted for the session's repository subscriptions.

With one spelling throughout the panel, the lowercasing in keyOf, which names a pull request for comparisons, and in cachePathOf, which finds the daemon's cached result, is redundant, so both now use the name as given. The panel's labels and the references it puts in the prompt now show repositories in lowercase. The CLI and the daemon already compare repositories without regard to case, so nothing outside hooks/ changes.

groups.title: The panel's readers lowercase each repository
groups.kicker: One spelling for each repository, set where the panel reads it
intro: Every pull request the panel shows enters through parseTracked, parseSubscriptions, or parseAdopted. Lowercasing there gives each repository one spelling for everything downstream. That covers the row labels, the GitHub query, which groups pull requests by repository, and the daemon's cache path. It also covers files that an earlier version wrote in mixed case.

A TrackedPr is the panel's reference to one pull request: a repo and a number. Its type does not enforce lowercase, so the rule holds only while nothing builds a TrackedPr outside the parsers. The type's comment now records that rule.

checks.text: Every TrackedPr in hooks/register.tsx and hooks/github.ts comes from one of the three parsers. subscribedOf builds its entries from parsed lines, and toPullRequest copies the parsed repo. Traced by reading every use of keyOf, cachePathOf, and TrackedPr.

The CLI and the daemon still agree with the panel. The daemon files its cache under repo.lower() and keys adopted pull requests by the lowercased repository. project watch drop and project loop drop, which Dismiss now runs with the lowercased name, compare repositories case-insensitively. Checked in watch.py and loop.py.

files.note: The three parsers lowercase repo. keyOf, cachePathOf, and the adopted-review match in subscribedOf stop lowercasing, because their inputs already are.

checks.text: keyOf no longer lowercases, so its two sides match only when both come from a parser. The inbox's match in register.tsx lowercases the item's reference before it compares it with keyOf.

groups.title: Tests for one repository in two spellings
groups.kicker: A panel test for the labels, and parser tests for each reader
intro: The new panel test tracks o/r#1 in one loop and O/R#2 in another. It expects the labels #1 and #2, and expects Discuss to insert #2 . The parser tests now expect each reader to return the repository in lowercase, and check that the daemon's cache path follows from a parsed subscription.
The fake GitHub in panel.test.tsx now looks repositories up without regard to case, as GitHub does.

checks.text: Each test can fail. In a copy of the head, removing the lowercasing from one parser at a time failed at least one test. Dropping it from parseTracked failed the new panel test and the parseTracked test, from parseSubscriptions three tests, and from parseAdopted the daemon's-files test.
